Folks — looping you in. Biolume pushed back and may only pre-fund $400k; they are asking for a 25% discount + full surcharge waiver.

Why this matters (business case):
- Fast revenue recognition (pre-fund applied as usage credits) and reduced CAC/time-to-first-dollar for Q3 activation.
- They are a strategic early adopter in therapeutics — high likelihood of expansion into embeddings + reranking in year two.
- Technical fit: they require VPC deployment which increases onboarding L2 work; we normally charge a 4% onboarding surcharge to offset that.

Options I see: 
A) Approve 25% discount + full surcharge waiver for $400k pre-fund (commercial win, faster close).
B) Approve 22% discount + surcharge waiver if customer increases to $450k pre-fund.
C) Counter with 18% discount + 1–2% surcharge (compromise).

Attachments included: biolume_pricing_proposal_v1.pdf, q3_usage_forecast.xlsx. HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/DL-2027-0587-BL

Ask: I don't have authority to approve >20% discount or full onboarding waiver. Can I get VP/CFO sign-off on one of the options above? Need a short authorization note we can push into the LOI/DocuSign. Timing: customer prefers decision this week; they can sign LOI by Aug 5 with a pre-fund target the following week.

Thanks — Aditya

Aditya — thanks for the clear options. A few finance questions before I sign off to Marissa: 

- Net ARR uplift: what is the expected recognized revenue in year 1 under each option (A/B/C)? The attached forecast doesn't separate pre-funded recognition vs consumed usage — can you produce a 12-month recognition table?
- Churn/credit risk: if they pre-fund and consume slower than forecast, do we allow credit carry-forward? My preference is no carry-forward beyond 90 days and no refunds.
- Surcharge rationale: since VPC onboarding requires engineer time, a partial surcharge protects delivery costs; if we waive fully we should include a one-time onboarding completion milestone tied to release of credits.

Quick commercial suggestions: 
- Counter to the customer with Option B (22% discount + full waiver) but only if they commit $450k pre-fund and accept a 90-day carry-forward cap.
- Alternatively offer Option A with a ramp clause: 25% for first 6 months then step down to 15% unless they hit usage thresholds.

I can draft the short approval memo for Marissa if you can deliver the revenue recognition table by EOD tomorrow.

Ben Carter
Director, Revenue Operations
